name: Pool cleaning
summary: Start a pool cleaning business: your first 25 people and partners, a price menu by pool size from real ranges, openings and closings where pools close for winter, and a visit log that checks each reading against CDC's ranges.
door_step3: I clean the pool and text you the readings
door_rule: Door hangers go on the door, never in or on a mailbox: putting unstamped flyers in a mailbox is a federal offense (18 U.S. Code 1725). Check your city rules on door to door flyers.

promises.quote: Pool size, service and how often in; a quote, a text and an invoice out.
promises.keep: A thank-you, an honest review ask, your regular plan, a referral ask and a later check-in, each dated, plus review cards with your QR code.

promises.proof: One pool turned into proof: a result card, a before-and-after collage from your photos, a caption, an honest review ask and a case study once they say yes.
promises.next_25: The next 25 pool supply stores, agents, HOAs, rental hosts and apartments near you that are not in your Pipeline yet, with messages, saved for Do my day.
promises.ready: Look ready before you reach out: a one-page website, a Google profile kit and a flyer, all from your real prices.
promises.same_street: One customer's street turned into a route: door hangers with a neighbor price, a sheet for the 20 nearest homes and an intro ask for your customer.
promises.season_plan: Twelve months of offers for where you live: closings and spring openings where pools close, the weekly route where they don't, with a calendar file.
promises.visit_log: Readings typed after a visit: a printable log, the text to the owner with what you did, and a flag on any reading outside CDC's ranges.

off_season.play: Where pools close for winter, sell closings in October and November, then book spring openings with a deposit from December. Where pools stay open all year, keep the weekly route full.

crowd.note: Pools in places like Florida, Phoenix and San Diego stay open all year. Up north most pools open in May or June and close in the fall.

Don't take on an apartment, condo or HOA pool before you check whether your state wants a certified operator.
Don't keep pool chemicals in a hot car or beside fuel. Store them dry, cool and apart, as CDC and EPA say.

items.item: Pool and spa contractor license (repairs and equipment)
items.what_to_check: Florida, as an example: repairing or replacing pool equipment, and any cleaning or equipment sanitizing that needs equipment partly taken apart (filter changes excepted), is licensed pool contractor work. Cleaning that doesn't affect the pool's structure or equipment, and water treatment that needs no such equipment, need no license there. Other states differ: check your state's contractor board before you repair or open up equipment.

sources.says: Commercial, residential and servicing pool/spa contractors: the scope includes the repair or replacement of existing equipment and any cleaning or equipment sanitizing that requires at least a partial disassembling, excluding filter changes. Water treatment that does not require such equipment does not require a license. In addition, a license is not required for the cleaning of the pool or spa in a way that does not affect the structural integrity of the pool or spa or its associated equipment.

items.item: Pools at apartments, condos, HOAs and hotels
items.what_to_check: In Florida a pool serving 5 or more living units (apartments, townhouses, subdivisions) or a hotel is a public pool. It needs an operating permit, and the state may require a certified pool service technician: a nationally recognized course or a pool contractor license counts. Condo and HOA pools of 32 units or fewer that aren't public lodging are exempt except for water quality. Check your state and county health department before you take one on.

sources.says: A public pool includes pools serving camps, churches, schools, subdivisions and cooperative living projects of five or more living units, such as apartments, hotels, motels and townhouses. A private pool is used only by an individual, family or living unit members and their guests and does not serve cooperative housing or joint tenancy of five or more living units.

Pools serving no more than 32 condominium or cooperative units, and pools serving homeowners associations with no more than 32 units or parcels, that are not operated as public lodging establishments are exempt from supervision under the chapter, except for water quality.
It is unlawful for any person or public body to operate or continue to operate any public swimming pool without a valid permit from the Department of Health.

The department may require that a public pool be serviced by a person certified as a pool service technician; anyone certified by a course of national recognition, or licensed under s. 489.105(3)(j), (k) or (l), is deemed certified. This does not apply to a person, or the direct employee of a person, permitted as a public pool operator.

items.item: Carrying pool chemicals in your vehicle
items.what_to_check: Chlorine products are oxidizers (EPA). The federal materials of trade rule (49 CFR 173.6) caps each package of a Class 8 or Division 5.1 material at 66 lb or 8 gallons (Packing Group II or III; 1 lb or 1 pint for Packing Group I) and 440 lb on one vehicle, in the maker's or an equally strong package, closed tight, secured against shifting and marked with a common name, and the driver must be told. Check each product's safety data sheet and your state's rules.

sources.says: Materials of trade: a Class 3, 8, 9, Division 4.1, 5.1, 5.2 or 6.1 material in a packaging of not over 30 kg (66 pounds) or 30 L (8 gallons) for Packing Group II or III, or 0.5 kg (1 pound) or 0.5 L (1 pint) for Packing Group I; packagings leak tight or sift proof, securely closed, secured against shifting, in the original or equally strong packaging and marked with a common name; the driver must be informed; no more than 200 kg (440 pounds) of materials of trade on one vehicle.

Chemicals that release chlorine, such as calcium hypochlorite, sodium hypochlorite and chlorinated isocyanurates, are classified as oxidizers. Keep chemicals dry, separate incompatible ones, handle one chemical at a time, and keep gasoline, oil and gas-powered equipment such as lawn mowers away from where they are stored.

items.what_to_check: Store them dry, apart from each other, in their original labeled containers, below 95 F, away from heat, flames, fuel and mowers, and out of reach of children and animals. Never mix chemicals; add chemical to water, never water to chemical; wear what the label calls for.

sources.says: Store pool chemicals below 95 F (35 C), each separately and incompatible chemicals away from each other, dry, in original manufacturer-labeled containers, away from heat sources and flames, and secured from children and animals.

steps: Before the first visit: written scope (skim, brush, vacuum, baskets, water test), how often, price per visit, which chemicals are included, the gate code, pets and who to call about equipment trouble.
On arrival: look over the pool, deck and equipment, and photograph anything broken or leaking before you start.
Skim the surface, brush walls and steps, then vacuum if it needs it.
Empty the skimmer and pump baskets, and note anything off at the filter or pump for the owner.
Test free chlorine and pH, a DPD kit is the most accurate, and log them in the Visit log card. Anything you add follows the product's label, one chemical at a time, never mixed.
Close gates and lids, take an after photo, and text the owner the readings and what you did.
Invoice or charge the card on file the same day; ask happy owners for an honest review.

sources.says: Pool service often includes skimming the pool, brushing the tile and steps, emptying skimmer and pump baskets, testing pool water and adjusting and adding chemicals as needed, vacuuming as needed, and backwashing a sand filter when the pressure is high. Radiance Pools: weekly logs and photos showing services performed or chemicals added to the pool during maintenance are emailed to the client.

Most professional pool cleaning services perform water testing and chemical balancing, skimming and surface cleaning, brushing walls and steps, vacuuming the pool floor, emptying pump and skimmer baskets, and an equipment inspection during their weekly routine.

advice.say: A green pool takes more time and chemicals, often more than one visit. Quote the cleanup on its own, then the weekly price once the water is clear. The green price is a judgment call: check current rates where you live.

Openings: ask when the pool was closed and whether the cover stayed on. A pool that grew algae over the winter needs a cleanup on top (Thumbtack), and one closed for years can cost $500 or more to open (Fixr).

Closings usually take two visits, because the water is shocked a few days ahead (Thumbtack, HomeAdvisor). Fixr: never drain a pool completely for winter; the water usually sits 3 to 6 inches below the skimmer.
Put them on the same day as the other pools on their street. Same street first keeps drive time down.
A chemical check visit is for owners who skim, brush and empty the baskets themselves. Write down who does what.

Filter cleaning: in Florida, cleaning that needs equipment partly taken apart is licensed contractor work, filter changes excepted (section 489.105). Check your state's rule before you open a filter housing.

street.headline: Free water test on {street}
includes: Free chlorine and pH tested with a DPD kit
how: Text me your address or scan the code
You get the readings by text
street.line: I'm cleaning a pool on {street}{day_part}, so the first 3 neighbors who text me get a free pool water test: chlorine and pH, about 10 minutes, readings by text. No cost and no catch.
street.post: Hi neighbors! I'm {first}, I run {business} here in {area}. I'm cleaning a pool on {street}{day_part}, so the first 3 neighbors who text me get a free water test (chlorine and pH, about 10 minutes, readings by text). No cost and no catch. {phone_line}
steps: Hang the door hangers on {street} the day before, on the door, never in or on a mailbox.
Test only with the owner home or their yes in writing, and never open a locked gate.
Log each test in the Visit log card and text the owner the readings. It never says how much of anything to add: that comes from the product's label.
Hand them the card with your weekly price before you leave, then one follow-up in 3 days.

pool_supply.eyebrow: For pool owners who shop at {biz}
pool_supply.headline: Weekly pool care, readings by text
pool_supply.card_line: Shop at {biz}? Mention them when you book.
steps: Walk in with the card and ask for the manager.
Offer the free first cleaning for one pool owner they pick, and log it in the Visit log card.
Ask to leave your cards at the counter.
Point the pool owners you work for to them for supplies and parts, and tell the manager you did.

realtors.demo: your next listing's pool cleaned free before the photos
realtors.headline: A clean pool before the listing photos
realtors.card_line: Listing with {biz}? Mention them when you book.
steps: Send the message and the card today, with two days you can do it.
Clean the pool before their listing photos, and take a photo from the deck before and after.
Send the photos to the agent the same day.
Ask once: would they leave your cards with sellers who have a pool?

hoas.demo: a free water test for 3 homeowners with backyard pools, on a day your manager picks
hoas.headline: Backyard pools kept clean, readings by text
hoas.card_line: Live in a community {biz} manages? Mention them when you book.
steps: Send the message and the card today.
Do the water tests only with the manager's yes and on the day they pick.
Text each owner their readings the same day, from the Visit log card.
This is for backyard pools. A community pool can fall under state health rules: check whether your state wants a certified operator before you quote one.

vacation_rentals.demo: one rental's pool cleaned free between guests, with the readings and a photo for your file
vacation_rentals.headline: The pool ready before every check-in
vacation_rentals.card_line: Rent through {biz}? Mention them when you book.
steps: Send the message and the card today.
Clean the sample pool between guests, on the day the manager picks, and log it in the Visit log card.
Send the readings and an after photo the same day.
A pool at a hotel or other lodging can count as a public pool: check your state and county health rules before you take on a route of rentals.

apartments.demo: a free water test at your community pool, with the readings written up for your file
apartments.headline: Your pool readings in writing, every visit
apartments.card_line: For the pool at {biz}: ask the manager.
steps: Send the message and the card today.
Test the water only with the manager there or their yes in writing, and log it in the Visit log card.
Send the readings the same day.
Before you quote any service, ask who holds the pool's operating permit, and check whether your state or county wants a certified pool operator or technician (Florida: sections 514.031 and 514.075).

same_street.neighbor_note: judgment call, not a sourced fact
same_street.headline: Your neighbor price on {street}
how: Text me your address or scan the code
same_street.customer_ask: Hi {customer}, thanks again! I'm adding a couple more pools on {street}{day_part}. If a neighbor ever asks who does your pool, would you pass on my number{phone_part}? It means a lot to a new business.
steps: Hang a door hanger on every home on this sheet the day before you are there. On the door, never in or on a mailbox.
While you work, say hi to anyone outside. Keep it short, and never say which neighbor: "I clean a pool here on your street."
Text your customer the intro ask after the visit, never before.
Mark each home on the sheet. A neighbor who books goes on the same day as your customer.
same_street.why: Pools on one street mean less driving between stops, so you can give neighbors a better price on the same day.

who.closing: Every pool you clean, then friends with pools
who.opening_book: This fall's closings first, then pool supply stores and agents
who.main: People you know with pools, neighbors of each customer, pool supply stores

do.closing: Text every pool on your route a closing date: Fixr says close when it is regularly below 65 F, before it freezes. Book their spring opening at the same visit.
do.opening_book: Book spring openings now with a small deposit, earliest dates first.
do.main: Fill each day of the week on one or two streets before you add a new area.

plans: Weekly pool service with routine chemicals included: the steady part of the year.
Closings in the fall and openings in spring where pools close for winter, booked a season ahead.
A first cleaning at the founding price: the offer that gets you to a new pool.
